newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Chance for upturn.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - Chance for upturn.

text.p: Gulf refined oil products have the first opportunity in the coming week to escape a summer lull if Asian markets trend higher and refinery maintainance in Saudi Arabia curbs supplies, Gulf traders said on Thursday.

Distillate premiums to independent price quotes remain seasonally weak, though a firmer Singapore, led higher by expectations of higher Indonesian and Chinese gas oil demand, served as a lauchpad for firmer Gulf premiums, traders said.
Gas oil, around $20.50 a barrel fob Gulf today, was at a 15-30 cents premium to the quote versus parity in mid July when outright prices fell to their lowest level since August 1995.
Kerosene, its spread to gas oil at $2.10-20, remained under pressure from good local supplies and lacklustre Asian and Far East demand, are was talked at a slight discount to the quote.
"September cargoes are in the frame...This should focus (buyers') minds on winter use," said one trader.

Fresh requirements from India Oil Corp (IOC) would also support. IOC have a September superior kerosene tender requirement but this alone was unlikely to push Gulf prices or premiums higher, traders said.
Saudi Aramco's 265,000 bpd Ras Tanura refinery is expected to enter 30-day maintenance from the second half of August.
The work will result in the shutdown of the plant's crude distillation unit (CDU), said industry sources.

Saudi Aramco this month sealed a deal with South Korean refiner Ssangyong to import 1.8 million barrels of gasoline over six months starting in July and has also been buying semi-term and spot cargoes to meet growing local demand and shortfalls created by increased Saudi naphtha exports.
"I can see more opprtunities to sell into Saudi (Arabia)," said one Gulf-based trader anticipating that Aramco would remain in the market for gasoline.
Others said Aramco had covered it light end requirements and that maintenance could provide support to middle distillate.
The impact of Iran's new 232,000 bpd Bandar Abbas refinery is starting to be felt in the spot market after initial commissioning of one of its two CDU commenced in June.
"It will take until next year before it is really ready but the effect will be noticeable this winter," said one trader.

Iran has traditionally increased its imports of heating fuels in the winter but a combination of higher runs at Bandar Abbas and products swap deals with Central Asian neighbours is expect to cap any imports.
It would potentially lead to Iranian gas oil exports in the fourth and first quarters.
NIOC has already began to market fuel oil exports for August after the start-up of the Bandar Abbas CDU which was now ran at 70,000 bpd, the Middle East Economic Survey reported this week.
Gulf crude differentials are expected to remain soft ahead of the expected resumption of Iraqi crude exports next month under the United Nations' "oil-for-food" deal.
Abu Dhabi grades talked at a 15-20 cents discount to official crude selling prices, Oman and Qatari grades at 30-35 cents discount.
